title: MV/MZ How do I add custom animations to sv enemies

posts.author: D_Draco
posts.body: I want to add animations to my enemies for example custom damage animations for each enemy and attack animations. Is there a plugin for this?

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
I take it you mean “motions” and not “animations”? It’s a matter of RPG Maker terminology, but the latter are the things that you show with “show animation”.
For adding more frames to motions, there’s a number of plugins available, but I guess you want advice on which one to use, since the plugins themselves are just a Google away. So in order to give some sensible advice, you’d need to tell us what your needs are. Every plug-in has its pros and cons.

posts.author: Anatis
posts.body:
The way I do this is (using RPG Maker MV, I believe the same is possible in MZ for the first half with Visustella plugins) : is with Yanfly's Animated Sideview Battlers plugin, alongside the Action Sequences packs for the Battle Core.
Mainly, I incorporate the enemy attack animations on their Spritesheet and call them through action sequences, using lines as per example:
motion idle: user
ani wait: 7
motion swing: user
ani wait: 7
motion skill: user
ani wait: 3
action effect
ani wait: 4
And so on. It takes quite a bit of getting used to and kind of "requires" you to keep a sheet with the motion names referencing to each portion of the sheet (which are...  counterintuitive) at hand for reference, and all these animations will be 2 frames of time for each frame so it's not the smoothest possible with the engine, which brings me to the second possibility which I also utilize and that's using the Animation System (this is possible in MV, not in MZ).
You can put the enemy frames in Animation Sheets and use the same plugins as mentioned before to "opacity user: 0%, 1" the enemy and fit it so that it appears to smoothly transition from the battlers actual graphic to the "copy" of that same image used in an Animation made in the database, I use this mainly for my enemy's Death animations but I also use it for some player skills as well.

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
So, as you might have gauged from
@Anatis
’s response, there’s two parts to what you want:
1. Adding frames (eg you want an idle motion with 4 frames instead of 3)
2. Action sequencing
There are several plugins for both, but there’s compatibility limitations between them. The tag says MV/MZ… Are you using MV or MZ?
In any case, I use
BattleMotionMZ
for the additional frames and VisuMZ_BattleCore for the action sequences. It takes a bit getting used to, but BattleMotionMZ allows for specifying:
number of frames for each motion individually
straight loop, pingpong loop, or no loop for each motion individually
chaining motions together
adding additional motions above the standard 18
